subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Walking Robots: Balancing on Legs
description: A 60-second lesson on Walking Robots: Balancing on Legs.

hook.text: Boston Dynamics' Spot walks over rubble, climbs stairs, and recovers from shoves. Wheels can't do that.

buildup.text: Each leg has three or more actuated joints. A balance controller adjusts foot placement hundreds of times per second.

discovery.text: Dynamic walking means the robot is always falling forward and catching itself. It's controlled falling, not static standing.

twist.text: Legs consume far more energy than wheels on flat ground. Walking robots trade efficiency for terrain adaptability.

climax.text: Disaster sites, construction zones, and forests are too rough for wheels. Legs go where wheels can't.

punchline.text: Wheels need roads. Legs just need ground.

quiz.question: What does 'dynamic walking' mean for a bipedal robot?
options: The robot locks each joint in place before taking the next step
The robot continuously falls forward and catches itself with each step
The robot uses wheels inside its feet to roll between steps
